wait_time: hours to days, depending on which route

steps.title: Work out which account you have
steps.detail: If you sign in to Fitbit with a Google account, your data comes through Google Takeout. If you still have a Fitbit account, use fitbit.com.

steps.title: For a Google account: open Takeout
steps.detail: Deselect all, then find the health product. It is now listed under Google Health rather than Fitbit, although the folders inside still say Fitbit.

steps.title: For a Fitbit account: fitbit.com, Settings, Data Export
steps.detail: You can choose a time period and a file format there, which Takeout does not offer.

steps.title: Request and wait
steps.detail: Heart rate at full resolution is by far the largest part and takes the longest to prepare.

steps.title: Expect thousands of small files
steps.detail: Heart rate is one file per day, and heart rate variability is a two-line file per day.

notes: The migration to Google created a second folder with the same metrics in a different format, so one export can contain both.
Sleep files are named after a date but each contains about a month of nights, in reverse order.
Exercise files are numbered in blocks of a hundred rather than dated, so there is no way to tell what is in one without opening it.

muletto_support.status: reads the per-day JSON into daily figures, taking every date from inside the record because the filenames lie - a sleep file holds a month of nights. Built from the documented layout; no real Fitbit export has been opened yet

faq.q: Where is Fitbit in Google Takeout?
faq.a: It is listed as Google Health rather than Fitbit. The folders inside the download still use the Fitbit name, which is why searching for it in the product list turns up nothing.

faq.q: Why does my Fitbit export have thousands of files?
faq.a: Heart rate is written one file per day, and heart rate variability one two-line file per day. Several years of wear produces several thousand files with very little in each.

faq.q: Can I get my Fitbit data without a Google account?
faq.a: Only if you still have a Fitbit login. Once the account is migrated, Takeout is the route.
